name: Triamcinolone injections

lead: Triamcinolone is a corticosteroid that dermatologists inject into patches of alopecia areata, an autoimmune cause of hair loss, to regrow hair in the patch. It is not used for ordinary pattern hair loss.

It is about five times as potent as cortisol and calms the local immune attack on follicles. A 2020 systematic review reported more than half regrowth in about 81 percent of treated patients, though hair often regrows on its own in patchy disease.

paras: It is given in a dermatologist's office as repeated injections into the bald patches, with regrowth judged over the following weeks to months.
It is prescription-only. Skin thinning is commonly described with skin injections, and injection near the eye has caused raised eye pressure and cases of endophthalmitis.

angle.text: Dermatologists inject triamcinolone into patches of alopecia areata to calm the immune attack on follicles so hair regrows in the patch. A 2020 review reported more than half regrowth in about 81 percent of treated patients.

lead: Triamcinolone acetonide is a synthetic glucocorticoid, about five times as potent as cortisol, sold under brand names such as Kenalog [1]. Injected into the skin (intralesional), it is used for inflammatory skin conditions and keloid scars, and dermatologists also use it for patchy alopecia areata, an autoimmune hair-loss condition [1][2].

A 2020 systematic review cited by Wikipedia found that about 81 percent of patients receiving 5 mg/mL triamcinolone injections achieved more than half regrowth [2]. Wikipedia also cautions that hair often regrows spontaneously in patchy disease, making treatment effects hard to judge [2]. The article is limited to appearance-relevant hair use; many other injection sites are medical uses unrelated to looks.

paras: For appearance, the main use is intralesional injection into patches of alopecia areata, and sometimes eyebrow loss, though Wikipedia says efficacy in small or eyebrow lesions is uncertain [2]. Intralesional triamcinolone is also used for hypertrophic scars and keloids [1][3]. Other medical routes include intra-articular, intravitreal and nasal products [1].

Wikipedia's drug article mentions raised eye pressure with intravitreal use and menstrual irregularities from progestogen-like activity [1]. Intravitreal use has been linked to noninfectious endophthalmitis [4]. Local skin thinning is a commonly described effect of skin injections in clinical sources but was not detailed in the pages loaded here.

A 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis (Yee et al.) summarized by Wikipedia reported more than 50 percent regrowth in about 81 percent of patients on 5 mg/mL injections [2]. Registered trials include a 2007 phase 2 study of adrenal function with intralesional triamcinolone 10 mg/mL in 18 patients with alopecia areata (NCT00484679) and a 2009 phase 2 study of combined Restylane and triamcinolone injections in 14 patients (NCT01797432); results are not summarized here [5][6]. A keloid comparison trial found intralesional verapamil and triamcinolone both used for scars [3].

lore.intro: Steroid scalp injections appear in discussions of alopecia areata and eyebrow thinning.
